messages:
asha: Heads up — after the RBAC roll last night we're seeing a SCIM deprovision loop hitting the provisioning service. KMS decrypt errors in the logs too. Started ~12:10 PDT. Anyone on call? :eyes:
ben: On it. Pasting the top error from provisioner logs:
```
 2026-03-21T19:10:12Z ERROR provisioner/scim.go:142 kms.Decrypt failed: InvalidCiphertext: decryption failed for key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef12-3456
    at github.com/redwood/provisioner/kms.(*Client).Decrypt
    at github.com/redwood/provisioner/scim.(*Handler).handleDelete
    ...
```
maria: We rotated the KMS alias idp-scim-key earlier today at 11:58 per rotation runbook. Any chance the service still points to the old key version?
ben: Checking env + k8s secret now. The provisioner is reading IDP_KMS_KEY_ARN from secret `idp-provisioner-secrets` in namespace idp-prod. Snippet: 
```
kubectl -n idp-prod get secret idp-provisioner-secrets -o yaml
# -> data.IDP_KMS_KEY_ARN: <redacted>
```
ben: I also see audit entries: DecryptFailed for that key at 11:59:01 from the key-rotation lambda. Might be a timing window where rotation happened but service not reloaded.
oncall: Okta is also returning 403 on some SCIM delete calls during retries: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{"errorCode":"E101","errorSummary":"Insufficient permissions to delete group membership"}
```
maria: The RBAC change added a wildcard-group cleanup rule that kicked the deprovisioner into a large delete sweep. If decrypts fail for the payloads (we encrypt delete payloads for verification), the deprovisioner retries and hits Okta rate-limits/403s. Combined = loop.
asha: Can we temporarily stop the deprovision sweep while we triage KMS?
ben: Yes — quick mitigation: scale the deprovisioner to zero and create a manual backlog for the affected users. Command: 
```
kubectl -n idp-prod scale deployment scim-deprovisioner --replicas=0
```
ben: I'm doing that now. Also reloading the provisioner pod will pick up the rotated key if the secret is updated.
asha: I'm also going to rollback the RBAC wildcard change to prevent more deletes. maria: I'll open a KMS support ticket to confirm key state and ask for previous key version access (we need a read fallback while we stabilize).
security-bot: Audit alert: kms:DecryptFailure logged 11:59:01 for key idp-scim-key by lambda:key-rotation (count 4) — creating incident:INC-2026-031
ben: After scaling down, I restarted one provisioner pod with the updated secret and watched logs — decrypt succeeded for a test payload. Looks like the issue was a pod that hadn't been restarted since rotation.
asha: Good. Plan from here: 1) keep deprovisioner scaled to 0, 2) roll back RBAC wildcard change, 3) reconcile Okta state (manual fixes), 4) restart scaled pods one-by-one and monitor decrypts + audit logs, 5) re-enable deprovisioner once stable.
maria: I'll run the rollback PR now and post links. PR: https://git.redwood.com/r/redwood/idp-config/pulls/487
oncall: Noted — I'll coordinate manual fixes with CS so no user outages.
ben: One follow-up action: add a graceful fallback in provisioner when Decrypt fails — surfacing a dead-letter queue instead of immediate retry + delete that requeues. File created: https://tracker.redwood.com/ISSUE-1123
asha: Agreed. Also add a runbook step: restart pods after KMS rotation and verify decrypts before enabling any mass SCIM runs.
security-bot: Reminder: record this sequence in audit logs and attach the KMS ticket number when incident is closed.
maria: PR merged and RBAC rollback applied. Monitoring decrypt/audit for 20m then we can re-enable deprovisioner if clean.
ben: 20m in — no DecryptFailure spikes, Okta 403s decreased. I'll scale scim-deprovisioner to 1 for a canary run.
asha: Thanks — ping when you see first successful batch.
ben: Canary succeeded (50 users), no errors. I'll continue ramp after another 30m. :thumbsup:
asha: Great job all.
